deadline.value: February 1, 2027 Fall application deadline on the Physics Department graduate admissions page (2025-2026 Graduate Bulletin also notes March 15 encouraged / rolling admission).
deadline.quote: The deadline for receipt of application materials for admission into the physics Ph.D. program is February 1.

also.quote: Application Deadline: Applications are encouraged by March 15 for Fall admission, but students can be admitted on a rolling basis.

gre_general.value: General GRE is not stated as required for the Physics Ph.D. (only the Physics GRE Subject Test is specified for external applicants).

gre_subject.value: Physics GRE Subject Test scores are required unless the applicant earned an M.S. in Physics from CMU (historically above the 50th percentile).
gre_subject.quote: Physics GRE scores if the applicant did not obtain an M.S. physics degree from CMU

supervisor.value: Admitted Physics Ph.D. students must have an approved faculty mentor, and the personal statement must identify a potential faculty mentor with whom the applicant should ideally have communicated beforehand.
supervisor.quote: Students admitted for a doctoral degree in physics must have a faculty mentor approved and financial support in the form of a teaching or research assistantship in place.

funding.value: Admitted Physics Ph.D. students must have a teaching or research assistantship in place, providing a competitive stipend, 20 credit hours of tuition waiver per academic year, and Michigan resident tuition classification.
funding.quote: Students admitted for a doctoral degree in physics must have a faculty mentor approved and financial support in the form of a teaching or research assistantship in place.

also.quote: Through an assistantship, you'll receive: A competitive stipend. 20 credit hours of tuition waiver for the academic year (unused hours may be used in the summer).

entry_route.value: Candidates are required to hold both Bachelor of Science (B.S.) and Master of Science (M.S.) degrees in physics or a related science (minimum 60 graduate credits beyond the M.S.).
entry_route.quote: Candidates are required to hold Bachelor of Science (B.S.) and Master of Science (M.S.) degrees in physics or a related area of science.

notes: 60-credit-hour post-M.S. Ph.D. in Physics covering astronomy/astrophysics, quantum science, nuclear physics, and theoretical/computational physics.
name: Ph.D. in Physics
